title: SOLO & CI TIROL Fest
subtitle: “Grounding and off ground: different perspectives to CI”

quick_facts.teachers: Maitane Sarralde, Pedro Penuela, Sarah Sea Clarke, Charlie Morrissey
quick_facts.format: Classes, Labs, Jams & Rock CI · Performances, Screenings & Talks

overview.manifesto_title: What does it mean to be grounded — as artists, as humans, as communities — and what happens when we let go of the ground?

concept_blocks.label: 01 / Physical & Philosophical Practice
concept_blocks.text:
In 2026, we look at Contact Improvisation as both a physical and philosophical practice — balancing between stability and flight, weight and suspension, presence and risk. Through movement, conversation, and shared reflection, we ask:
What does it mean to be grounded — as artists, as humans, as communities — and what happens when we let go of the ground?

This year’s program expands CI into new terrains — literally. Participants will have the opportunity to explore movement on the rock with a belay system, discovering new ways to connect gravity and improvisation in nature.

concept_blocks.label: 02 / Spaces for Dialogue
concept_blocks.text:
Beyond physical practice, the festival continues to open spaces for dialogue. We will host open talks with invited artists such as Pedro Penuela and Sarah Sea, who will lead conversations around sexuality, gender, identity, and body politics, inviting multiple perspectives on how we relate, move, and create together.

Motion Mode of Dialogue continues to be a space where art, movement, and social reflection meet — a place for connection, questioning, and discovery.

Join us for this journey between earth and air, grounding and flight, body and idea.

highlights: Daily CI classes, labs, and research sessions, jams with live music
Shared meals and informal gatherings in the heart of the Tirol mountains.

teachers.name: Maitane Sarralde
teachers.bio:
After graduating with a degree in Physical Activity and Sports Sciences, she began dancing through improvisation. In her final year of university, she studied dance from a creative and therapeutic perspective at the University of Human Motricity in Lisbon.

Since then, she has trained and devoted herself to the creation and performance of contemporary dance, integrating circus, martial arts, and Contact Improvisation. In 2020, she founded her company to explore new approaches to harness dance, the intrinsic narrative of detachment, and the physics of suspended bodies.

classes.title: Vertical Dance in Nature
classes.label: WORKSHOP
classes.desc: In this vertical dance workshop, we will work with chest harnesses and semi-static rope on a wall between 10-14m high. It will be an introduction to vertical dance on the wall from a healthy and conscious place. We will use the vertical supports of the wall/rock and the harness to understand our bodies in other planes where we can dance in dialogue with the inertia of the pendulum and the sensation of hanging or anti-gravity.

teachers.name: Pedro Penuela
teachers.bio: Pedro Penuela is a dancer, psychologist and PhD in performing arts from Brazil, currently based in Greece. In his PhD he researched forms of presence in the works of Steve Paxton, Pina Bausch and Kazuo Ohno, having had the opportunity of interviewing Paxton twice. He has been dancing and practicing Contact Improvisation since 2006, having studied with many teachers including Nita Little, Ray Chung, Daniel Lepkoff, Otto Ramstad, Lisa Nelson, and Karen Nelson.

classes.title: Action-Non-Action
classes.label: WORKSHOP
classes.desc:
“Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.” — Lao Tzu (Dao de jing)

In this workshop we will explore connections between the practice of CI and the Taoist principle of Wei wu wei (wu wei), freely translated as 'action without action'. Wu wei means moving in deep attunement with the wider flow of changing events. We will focus on sensing the ongoing life of our organs, investigating layers of contact, and deepening listening.

classes.title: The Issue of Sexuality in CI
classes.label: LECTURE & SHARED DISCUSSION
classes.desc: Sexuality is a topic widely raised and discussed throughout the decades of development of Contact Improvisation. How do we conceive and think nowadays about sexuality and its implications and overlaps with CI? What are our experiences regarding consent, safe spaces, inclusivity and diversity? We will read fragments from Contact Quarterly and engage in guided small-group and circle discussions.

teachers.name: Sarah Sea Clarke
teachers.bio: Sarah Sea Clarke brings an engaged sociopolitical and somatic approach to Contact Improvisation, examining inclusivity, queer identity, and touch cultures in somatic practice across Europe.

classes.title: Cultivating a Sense of/for CI
classes.label: WORKSHOP
classes.desc: In this two-part workshop we will research our senses and how bringing attention to them might enrich our CI dance practice. We isolate the different senses of sound, sight and touch for deeper awareness of the present moment, including grounding work, embodied meditation techniques and deep listening.

classes.title: Contact Improv and the Somatics Family Tree
classes.label: OPEN TALK & PARTICIPATORY LECTURE
classes.desc: Originating at a time in the United States that rejected hierarchical structures in dance, CI drew from embodiment and neo-phenomenological approaches. In this talk and participatory deliberation, we create our very own CI and Somatics family tree exploring CI as a force for change and collective healing.

teachers.name: Charlie Morrissey
teachers.bio: Charlie is a performer, teacher, collaborator and director who has been working with movement for more than 35 years. His work is inspired by long-term relationships with Steve Paxton, Lisa Nelson, Kirstie Simson, and Siobhan Davies. He co-curates Wainsgate Dances in Yorkshire, UK.

classes.title: The Apple Returns to the Tree
classes.label: WORKSHOP
classes.desc: Referencing Steve Paxton’s musings about the Newtonian apple as it falls from the tree, we return to the basic propositions of CI: noticing ourselves as masses in relation to physical forces, falling and rising, bouncing and tumbling anew with materials developed with Paxton and Nelson.

performances.title: Hacer Sonar El Aire
performances.desc: A breathtaking vertical dance performance on the medieval facade of the Innsbruck City Tower, interacting with architecture, wind, and audience gaze.

performances.title: Grounding – Off Ground
performances.desc: An experimental improvisation performance exploring themes of terrestrial contact and weightlessness within the minimalist white-cube space of WEISSRAUM.
